===== BEGIN H42_design.txt =====
H42 frozen 2026-11-18 23:39:01 UTC. Patch SHA256 8af619b4290f57812a33dae3bbea4dad13e86098418aba82d384e10d1d0abd5d.
Exact hunk is qsearch in-check HistRework eager map generation replaced by ready=0 lazy reset, not all threat-map readers generally. Diagnostic creates node-local RAII context at this reset site, active only in_check&&HistRework. Saves fresh original unconditional pawn/minor/rook unions in stack context, without calling instrumented lesser_threats/H71. Context saves Board address, key and ply; every reader requires all three to match. QuietScorer explicitly stores its construction ply for this comparison. Nested qsearch contexts restore previous context on destruction; unrelated nodes/plies do not count as matches.
One use per matching consumed piece-specific mask at QuietScorer.score (reader0), quiet_history (reader1), rework_entry (reader2). Compare actual full mask with saved eager reference, not a ready flag or recomputed cached value. White-only WRONG15 toggles bit0 of private expectedmask, leaves actual mask/history/oldcounters unchanged. White/Black, reader, and piece-family pawnminor/rook/queen/kingempty are separate partitions of uses.
At scope destruction, separate read/unread scope counters record whether any matched consumption occurred. Unread scopes are unobserved, not successful uses. One scope may yield multiple mask reads. Lazy-reference generation does not itself count as a use. Reference computed only once per enabled qsearch node before consumers, not once per unrelated reader.
Shares attack tables, board representation and old map formulas; no independent attack legality proof. Checks observed qsearch-node consumer state after reset, not every fullsearch invalidation or all future reader paths. No extra history mutation, Board move, NNUE evaluation or old counter hook. Existing H71 generation counts should remain unchanged.

===== END H42_design.txt =====

 namespace forge {
 
+#if FORGE_SHORTCUT_COUNT
+namespace {
+struct H42Context;
+thread_local H42Context* h42_current=nullptr;
+struct H42Context {
+    H42Context* previous;
+    const Board* board;
+    std::uint64_t key;
+    int ply;
+    b4::LesserThreats reference;
+    bool enabled,read=false;
+    H42Context(const Board& b,int p,bool on):previous(h42_current),board(&b),key(b.key()),ply(p),enabled(on) {
+        h42_current=on?this:nullptr;
+        if(!on)return;
+        const Color them=opposite(b.side_to_move());
+        const Bitboard occ=b.occupied();
+        const Bitboard pawn=pawn_attacks_bb(them,b.pieces(them,Pawn));
+        reference.by_type[Pawn]=reference.by_type[Knight]=reference.by_type[Bishop]=pawn;
+        Bitboard minor=pawn;
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Knight);bb;)minor|=attacks::knight(pop_lsb(bb));
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Bishop);bb;)minor|=attacks::bishop(pop_lsb(bb),occ);
+        reference.by_type[Rook]=minor;
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Rook);bb;)minor|=attacks::rook(pop_lsb(bb),occ);
+        reference.by_type[Queen]=minor;
+    }
+    ~H42Context(){if(enabled)shortcut_count::scope_h42(read);h42_current=previous;}
+};
+void h42_consume(const Board& board,int ply,int pt,Bitboard actual,int reader) {
+    H42Context* c=h42_current;
+    if(!c || c->board!=&board || c->ply!=ply || c->key!=board.key())return;
+    c->read=true;
+    Bitboard expected=c->reference.by_type[static_cast<std::size_t>(pt)];
+#if FORGE_SHORTCUT_WRONG15
+    if(board.side_to_move()==White)expected^=Bitboard{1};
+#endif
+    const int piecegroup=pt==Rook?1:(pt==Queen?2:((pt==King||pt==NoPieceType)?3:0));
+    shortcut_count::record_h42(actual!=expected,board.side_to_move()==White,reader,piecegroup,board);
+}
+}
+#endif
+
 int DrawJitter = 0;

===== BEGIN H33_design.txt =====
H33 opens kF src/search.cpp1819-1829. The newly cached material-count index uses validity bit8; surrounding nonpawn-cache, material-mix and NNUE metadata lines are context, not all proved by this counter.
One use per record_move after child->corr_valid assignment and before NNUE-disabled early return. Independently copy square-array board and apply the move with existing piece_reference::after, handling destination capture, EP removed pawn, promotion replacement and castling rook relocation. Count White/Black Pawn..Queen from square arrays before/after. Expected child bit8valid = parent bit8valid AND identical countvectors. Compare actual child bit8 validity. For actual-valid child only, compare index with freshly hashed postmove square counts using original material_key constants/mask. Invalid payload intentionally unspecified and ignored.
This checks transition even if no later correction-history consumer uses the child. It differs from H36's selected consumer index check. Reference makes no Board move, mutates no actual cache, and invokes no old counted hooks. Shares piece_reference copy/after and move semantics with earlier independent diagnostics; not a standalone chess-law oracle. Counter covers only material-index valid bit and valid payload, not nonpawn-index/material-mix/metadata transitions or arbitrary malformed moves.
Classes White/Black, parent_valid/invalid, count_changed/unchanged, child_valid/invalid independently partition uses. Moveclass partition priority EP, then promotion (including promotion capture), then ordinary capture, else quiet (including castle). Classes derive flags, while validity reference derives actual square countvector changes.
WRONG15 flips only private expected-valid Boolean on White-to-move transitions. This affects one reachable class without touching real child cache or fresh index. Control must show White uses strict subset. Old25 counts and strict canonical final-info values except time/nps must remain exact per search. No reference native test was run before prediction.

===== END H33_design.txt =====

===== BEGIN H33_cross_review.txt =====
H33 read-only review 2026-11-18 23:40 UTC.
Opened staging record_move diagnostic and piece_reference::after. Reference copies square array and applies EP removed-square, promotion replacement and orthodox castling rook move without Board::make_move. Ten per-color Pawn-through-Queen counts yield expected valid=parentvalid&&materialcountsunchanged. Original actual uses captured/promotion conditions, so reference does not duplicate that condition. Fresh post-move hash order is White then Black, Pawn..Queen with original arithmetic.
Actual bit8 checked; copied payload compared only if actual valid. Invalid cache payload unobservable and not semantically compared. White-only private expected-valid flip changes no actual state. No old counter hook or helper mutation. Shared square-array helper, orthodox castling assumptions and hash constants remain scope limits; not every nonpawn-cache or NNUE transition proven. No source edits or native experiments in this review.

+struct H42Context;

+struct H42Context {
+    H42Context* previous;
+    const Board* board;
+    std::uint64_t key;
+    int ply;
+    b4::LesserThreats reference;
+    bool enabled,read=false;
+    H42Context(const Board& b,int p,bool on):previous(h42_current),board(&b),key(b.key()),ply(p),enabled(on) {
+        h42_current=on?this:nullptr;
+        if(!on)return;
+        const Color them=opposite(b.side_to_move());
+        const Bitboard occ=b.occupied();
+        const Bitboard pawn=pawn_attacks_bb(them,b.pieces(them,Pawn));
+        reference.by_type[Pawn]=reference.by_type[Knight]=reference.by_type[Bishop]=pawn;
+        Bitboard minor=pawn;
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Knight);bb;)minor|=attacks::knight(pop_lsb(bb));
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Bishop);bb;)minor|=attacks::bishop(pop_lsb(bb),occ);
+        reference.by_type[Rook]=minor;
+        for(Bitboard bb=b.pieces(them,Rook);bb;)minor|=attacks::rook(pop_lsb(bb),occ);
+        reference.by_type[Queen]=minor;
+    }
+    ~H42Context(){if(enabled)shortcut_count::scope_h42(read);h42_current=previous;}
+};
+void h42_consume(const Board& board,int ply,int pt,Bitboard actual,int reader) {
+    H42Context* c=h42_current;
+    if(!c || c->board!=&board || c->ply!=ply || c->key!=board.key())return;
